hacker_news.title: Show HN: Genesis Map – Visualize your agent's changes. See where they can break
hacker_news.description: When agent ships code faster and faster, human review is no longer possible. Which brings 2 problems, at least for me: 1. I need to understand what my agent changes as quickly and easily as possible, cuz I don't wanna lose track of the current status of my product, or be the main bottleneck in shipping code. 2. I don't trust what my agent tells me. Many times, I've been suffered from agent telling me "all is well", then say "you are right, sorry, I missed..." after code failed on production. To mitigate those problems, I made Genesis, a skill for coding agent to generate a beautiful flow chart to understand all the business flows, flag all risk changes and untested code between commits. It worked very well on me, so I benchmarked it against vanilla Claude code and Codex: Vanilla → With Genesis 1. Test gaps caught: Claude Code 8% → 38% · Codex 4% → 23% 2. False alarms per review: Claude Code 2.1 → 0.7 · Codex 1.4 → 0.5 3. Real risks found per review: Claude Code 2.9 → 2.8 · Codex 2.4 → 2.4

hacker_news.title: NariQ: BF16-level Qwen3.8-27B in a 10 GB file
hacker_news.description: We built NariQ: 3-bit-or-lower quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B that retain near-BF16 quality across agentic tasks, math, multilingual reasoning, and image understanding. To our knowledge, this is the first 3-bit-or-lower quantization that retains BF16 lvl performance on long-horizon agentic tasks. Benchmarks (BF16 / 3-bit / 2.5-bit / 2-bit): - DeepSWE: 39.8 / 41.0 / 41.9 / 28.6 - Terminal-Bench 2.1: 62.6 / 63.8 / 60.2 / 52.4 - AIME 25+26: 97.7 / 98.3 / 96.5 / 86.0 - MSGM: 94.0 / 93.1 / 91.8 / 90.6 - RealWorldQA: 82.4 / 82.4 / 81.3 / 80.9 Decode speed is comparable to other quants on an RTX PRO 6000. Context-length results below (3-bit / 2.5-bit / 2-bit / Unsloth UD-IQ3_XXS): - 4K: 88.9 / 99.2 / 111.7 / 94.7 - 16K: 84.5 / 93.8 / 105.1 / 89.8 - 64K: 70.7 / 77.5 / 85.0 / 74.8 Running these currently require our llama.cpp fork: ( https://github.com/nari-labs/nari-llama.cpp ) Feedback and questions welcome. We'd love to hear how these perform on your workloads.
